examples.ko: 이번 회의에서 그 문제를 종결짓고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to bring that issue to a close at this meeting.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 노래 한 곡으로 공연을 종결지었어요.
examples.en: The singer ended the concert with one last song.
I apologized first to put an end to the argument.

examples.ko: 이 논의는 오늘 안에 종결지을 수 없을 것 같아요.
examples.en: I don't think we can wrap up this discussion today.

examples.ko: 사건을 빨리 종결짓지 말고 더 알아봐요.
examples.en: Let's not close the case too quickly; let's look into it more.

examples.ko: 두 나라는 오랜 갈등을 종결짓기로 했어요.
examples.en: The two countries decided to put an end to their long conflict.

explain: '끝내다'보다 딱딱해서 논쟁, 회의, 사건처럼 길게 이어진 일을 매듭지을 때 어울려요. 'ㅅ' 불규칙이라 '종결지어요', '종결지으면'으로 바뀌어요. 말할 때는 '마무리 짓다', '끝내다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is stiffer than '끝내다' and fits things that dragged on, such as debates, meetings and cases. It is a ㅅ-irregular verb, so it becomes '종결지어요' and '종결지으면'. In casual talk, '마무리 짓다' or '끝내다' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 사람마다 종교관이 달라서 이야기할 때 조심해요.
examples.en: Everyone's religious views differ, so I'm careful when I talk about it.

examples.ko: 제 종교관은 부모님의 영향을 많이 받았어요.
examples.en: My religious views were greatly influenced by my parents.
My religious views changed little by little as I traveled.

examples.ko: 이 소설에는 작가의 종교관이 잘 드러나요.
examples.en: The author's religious views show clearly in this novel.
It is important to respect each other's religious views.
I had a long discussion with my friend about our religious views.

explain: '세계관', '인생관', '가치관'처럼 '-관'으로 끝나는 말과 한 묶음으로 기억하면 좋아요. 일상 대화에서는 '종교에 대한 생각'이라고 풀어서 말하는 경우도 많아요.
explain_en: Remember it together with words ending in '-관' such as '세계관', '인생관' and '가치관'. In daily talk, people often say '종교에 대한 생각' (thoughts about religion) instead.

examples.en: He never told the truth in the end.
I waited, but news never came in the end.
The two of them never made up in the end.
That promise was never kept in the end.

examples.ko: 노인은 종내 고향 땅을 밟지 못했어요.
examples.en: The old man never set foot in his hometown again.

examples.ko: 종내 비는 그치지 않고 밤까지 내렸어요.
examples.en: The rain never stopped and kept falling until night.

explain: '끝내'와 뜻이 비슷하지만 글, 뉴스, 소설에서 주로 써요. 뒤에 '못하다', '않다' 같은 부정 표현이 오면 '끝까지 ~하지 않았다'는 아쉬운 느낌이 나요. 대화에서는 '끝내'나 '결국'이 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is close to '끝내' but is mostly used in writing, news and novels. With a negative like '못하다' or '않다', it carries a feeling of 'never did, even in the end', often with regret. In conversation, '끝내' or '결국' sounds more natural.

examples.en: When spring comes, larks sing in the fields.
Larks sing while flying high in the sky.
I saw a picture of a lark in a storybook.
My little sister, chattering like a lark since morning, is cute.

examples.ko: 저 새가 종달새인지 아닌지 잘 모르겠어요.
examples.en: I'm not sure whether that bird is a lark or not.

examples.ko: 종달새 소리에 아침 일찍 잠에서 깼어요.
examples.en: I woke up early in the morning to the sound of a lark.

explain: 봄 풍경을 그린 시나 동요에 잘 어울리는 새예요. 같은 새를 '종다리'라고도 하지만 보통은 '종달새'라고 해요. 명랑하게 재잘대는 모습을 종달새에 빗대어 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: This bird fits poems and children's songs about spring scenery. The same bird is also called '종다리', but people usually say '종달새'. Cheerful chattering is sometimes compared to a lark.

examples.en: Our company holds its year-end ceremony on December 30.

examples.ko: 종무식에서 사장님이 한 해 동안 수고했다고 말씀하셨어요.
examples.en: At the year-end ceremony, the president said we had worked hard all year.
After the year-end ceremony, I had lunch with my team.
This year's year-end ceremony will be held online.

examples.ko: 종무식 때 받은 작은 선물이 마음에 들어요.
examples.en: I like the small gift I got at the year-end ceremony.
Once the year-end ceremony is over, the year-end holiday begins.

explain: 한 해의 마지막 근무일에 하는 행사예요. 새해 첫 근무일에 하는 '시무식'과 짝을 이루는 말이에요. 회사나 관공서 이야기에서 주로 들을 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is the event held on the last working day of the year, and it pairs with '시무식', held on the first working day of the new year. You mostly hear it in talk about companies and offices.

examples.ko: 경기가 종반으로 접어들자 응원 소리가 커졌어요.
examples.en: As the game entered its final stage, the cheering got louder.
The drama reached its final phase and the story sped up.

examples.ko: 선거 운동도 이제 종반을 향하고 있어요.
examples.en: The election campaign is now heading into its last stage.
A comeback goal came late in the game and I was surprised.

examples.ko: 시험 준비가 종반이라 요즘 더 바빠요.
examples.en: My exam prep is in its final stretch, so I'm busier these days.
The ending part of this movie was a little disappointing.

explain: 반대말은 '초반'이고, 가운데는 '중반'이라고 해요. 경기, 드라마, 선거처럼 진행되는 일의 끝부분에 써요. '막바지'와 비슷한데 '종반'이 더 딱딱해서 뉴스나 중계에서 많이 들려요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '초반' (early stage), and the middle is '중반'. It is used for the last part of something in progress, like a game, drama or election. It is close to '막바지', but '종반' is more formal and common in news and commentary.

examples.ko: 두 회사는 종속적인 관계가 아니라 대등한 사이예요.
examples.en: The two companies are equals, not in a subordinate relationship.

examples.ko: 아이를 부모에게 종속적인 존재로 보면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't see a child as someone subordinate to their parents.

examples.ko: 이 나라는 경제가 너무 종속적이라서 걱정이에요.
examples.en: This country's economy is too dependent, which is worrying.

examples.ko: 종속적인 태도로는 좋은 관계를 만들기 어려워요.
examples.en: It is hard to build a good relationship with a subservient attitude.

examples.ko: 그 직원은 상사에게 종속적이라는 말을 들어요.
examples.en: That employee is said to be overly dependent on the boss.

examples.ko: 이 프로그램은 특정 기계에 종속적이지 않아요.
examples.en: This program is not tied to any particular machine.

explain: 사전에는 관형사로 나오지만 실제로는 '종속적인 관계', '종속적이다'처럼 '인/이다'를 붙여 많이 써요. 반대말은 '독립적'이에요. 사람이나 나라, 프로그램처럼 다른 것에 매여 있는 상태를 말할 때 쓰고, 좋은 뜻은 아니에요.
explain_en: Dictionaries list it as a determiner, but in practice it is used as '종속적인 관계' or '종속적이다' with '인/이다'. Its opposite is '독립적' (independent). It describes a person, country or program tied to something else, and it is not a positive word.

en: the eldest grandson of the head family

examples.en: The head grandson of our family is my cousin.
My eldest brother, the head grandson, prepares the ancestral rites.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 종손이 집안을 이끌어야 한다고 하셨어요.
examples.en: Grandfather said the head grandson should lead the family.
The whole family was happy when the head grandson was born.
He is the head grandson of this family.
Some families hand down the family register to the head grandson.

explain: 요즘은 쓰는 집이 줄었지만 명절이나 제사 이야기에서 들을 수 있어요. 집안의 맏이 쪽인 '종가'와 함께 알아 두면 좋고, 종손의 아내는 '종부'라고 해요. 보통 집안의 큰손자는 '장손'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Fewer families use it now, but you can hear it when people talk about holidays and ancestral rites. It is good to learn it with '종가' (the head family), and the head grandson's wife is called '종부'. An ordinary eldest grandson is usually called '장손'.

examples.en: The baby is babbling something to itself.

examples.ko: 동생이 하루 종일 종알거려서 정신이 없어요.
examples.en: My little brother chatters all day long and I can't think.
I can hear the kids chattering in the back seat.

examples.ko: 딸이 학교 이야기를 종알거리며 집에 들어왔어요.
examples.en: My daughter came home chattering about school.
If you keep chattering during class, your friends get disturbed.
My nephew chattering to his doll is cute.

explain: 주로 아이처럼 작고 귀여운 목소리로 쉬지 않고 재잘댈 때 써요. '종알대다', '종알종알하다'와 거의 같고, '중얼거리다'는 혼잣말을 낮은 소리로 하는 느낌이라 서로 달라요.
explain_en: It is mostly used when someone, like a child, chatters nonstop in a small, cute voice. It is almost the same as '종알대다' and '종알종알하다', but '중얼거리다' means muttering to oneself in a low voice, so it is different.

examples.en: The child babbles away next to her mother.
My granddaughter walks along chattering about kindergarten.
What are you chattering on about?

examples.ko: 동생은 말문이 트이자 쉬지 않고 종알댔어요.
examples.en: Once my little brother started talking, he chattered nonstop.
I woke up to the sound of chattering from early morning.
The child who had been chattering suddenly went quiet.

explain: '종알거리다'와 뜻이 같아서 바꿔 써도 돼요. '-거리다'와 '-대다'는 둘 다 같은 행동이 반복되는 느낌을 더해 줘요. 귀엽게 보는 말투라서 어른에게는 놀리는 느낌이 날 수 있어요.
explain_en: It means the same as '종알거리다' and you can swap them. Both '-거리다' and '-대다' add a feeling of repeated action. It has an affectionate tone, so using it for adults can sound teasing.

examples.en: The child chatters on about her day.

examples.ko: 동생은 차 안에서 종알종알 쉬지 않고 말했어요.
examples.en: My little brother chattered nonstop in the car.
My daughter talks in a chattering, singsong way.
The baby babbles away.

examples.ko: 퇴근하자마자 아내가 종알종알 오늘 있었던 일을 들려줬어요.
examples.en: As soon as I got home, my wife chattered about what happened today.

examples.ko: 종알종알 떠드는 소리가 방 안에서 들려요.
examples.en: I can hear chattering voices from inside the room.

explain: 작고 귀여운 소리로 말이 계속 이어지는 모습이에요. 큰 소리로 떠들 때는 '왁자지껄', 알아듣기 어렵게 낮게 말할 때는 '중얼중얼'이 어울려요.
explain_en: It describes talk that keeps flowing in a small, cute voice. For loud noisy chatter, '왁자지껄' fits better, and '중얼중얼' fits low, hard-to-understand muttering.

examples.en: The child chatters until late at night.

examples.ko: 동생이 옆에서 종알종알하는 바람에 책을 못 읽었어요.
examples.en: My little brother kept chattering beside me, so I couldn't read.

examples.ko: 딸은 신이 나면 계속 종알종알하곤 해요.
examples.en: My daughter often keeps chattering when she's excited.
The baby is playing by itself, babbling away.
What were you chattering about so much?
The chattering sound suddenly stopped.

explain: '종알거리다', '종알대다'와 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. 아이나 귀여운 사람이 쉬지 않고 말하는 모습에 어울려서, 어른에게 쓰면 조금 놀리는 느낌이 날 수 있어요.
explain_en: You can swap it with '종알거리다' and '종알대다'. It suits a child or a cute person talking nonstop, and using it for adults can sound a bit teasing.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 은퇴는 한 시대의 종언이라고 불렸어요.
examples.en: The singer's retirement was called the end of an era.
The newspaper covered the end of the Cold War at length.

examples.ko: 오랜 갈등이 종언을 고하고 평화가 찾아왔어요.
examples.en: The long conflict came to an end and peace arrived.

examples.ko: 많은 사람이 종이 신문의 종언을 이야기해요.
examples.en: Many people talk about the end of paper newspapers.

examples.ko: 그 공장이 문을 닫은 것은 마을 산업의 종언이었어요.
examples.en: The factory's closing was the end of the town's industry.

examples.ko: 이 협정은 전쟁의 종언을 뜻하지 않아요.
examples.en: This agreement does not mean the end of the war.

explain: '끝'보다 훨씬 딱딱해서 뉴스나 논설에서 '종언을 고하다'처럼 나와요. 시대, 제도, 흐름처럼 큰 것이 끝날 때 어울리고, 개인의 작은 일에는 잘 안 써요. 일상에서는 그냥 '끝'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is much stiffer than '끝' and appears in news and editorials as '종언을 고하다'. It suits the end of big things like eras, systems or trends, not small personal matters. In daily life people just say '끝'.

examples.ko: 골목이 어두워서 어디가 어딘지 종잡을 수 없어요.
examples.en: The alley is dark, so I can't tell where is where.

examples.ko: 그 사람 말이 너무 복잡해서 종잡기 어려워요.
examples.en: What he says is so complicated that it's hard to make sense of.

examples.ko: 날씨가 변덕스러워서 내일 일을 종잡지 못하겠어요.
examples.en: The weather is so fickle that I can't predict tomorrow.

examples.ko: 아이의 속마음을 종잡아 보려고 천천히 물어봤어요.
examples.en: I asked slowly to try to figure out what the child really felt.

examples.ko: 이야기가 갑자기 바뀌어서 무슨 뜻인지 종잡을 수가 없었어요.
examples.en: The story changed suddenly and I couldn't grasp what it meant.

examples.ko: 처음 온 도시라 방향을 종잡지 못해서 지도를 봤어요.
examples.en: It was my first time in the city and I couldn't get my bearings, so I looked at a map.

explain: 거의 '종잡을 수 없다', '종잡기 어렵다'처럼 부정이나 어려움과 함께 써요. '종잡을 수 없는 사람'은 무슨 생각을 하는지 알 수 없는 사람이에요. '갈피를 잡을 수 없다'와 비슷하게 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is almost always used with a negative or difficulty, as in '종잡을 수 없다' or '종잡기 어렵다'. A '종잡을 수 없는 사람' is someone whose thoughts you can't read. It can be used much like '갈피를 잡을 수 없다'.

examples.en: When it started to rain, people hurried off with quick short steps.
The child trots along after her mother.
Afraid of being late, I hurried to the station in quick little steps.
Grandmother came out to meet us in quick little steps.

examples.ko: 종종걸음 치는 모습이 귀여워서 웃음이 났어요.
examples.en: Seeing the little trotting steps was so cute that I laughed.
It's closing time, so everyone is hurrying along.

explain: '종종걸음을 치다', '종종걸음으로 가다'처럼 써요. 큰 보폭으로 힘차게 걷는 '성큼성큼'과 반대로, 작은 보폭으로 바삐 걷는 모습이에요. '총총걸음'과 거의 같아요.
explain_en: It is used as '종종걸음을 치다' or '종종걸음으로 가다'. It is the opposite of '성큼성큼' (long, bold strides) and describes hurrying in small steps. It is nearly the same as '총총걸음'.

en: home country of a sport or culture; country of origin

examples.en: Korea is the home country of taekwondo in the world.
It's even more special because the tournament is held in the sport's home country.
They say England is the birthplace of football.
Athletes from the home country won many gold medals.

examples.ko: 종주국의 자존심을 지켜야 한다고 감독이 말했어요.
examples.en: The coach said we have to protect the pride of the home country.
It's interesting that every sport has a different country of origin.

explain: '태권도 종주국'처럼 운동이나 문화가 처음 시작된 나라를 가리킬 때 가장 많이 써요. '원조'는 사람이나 가게에도 쓰지만 '종주국'은 나라에만 써요. 옛 뜻은 다른 나라를 속국으로 거느린 나라, 곧 종주권을 가진 나라예요.
explain_en: It is most often used, as in '태권도 종주국', for the country where a sport or culture began. '원조' can be used for people or shops, but '종주국' is used only for countries. The older meaning is a country that holds suzerainty over a dependent state.

examples.en: Please put a little soy sauce in the small dish.
Could you take out two small dishes?
I put the chili vinegar sauce in a small dish and set it on the table.

examples.ko: 식당에서 종지 하나를 더 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: I asked the restaurant for one more small dish.

examples.ko: 종지가 작아서 소스가 넘칠 것 같아요.
examples.en: The dish is small, so the sauce might overflow.

examples.ko: 할머니는 깨진 종지를 버리지 않고 화분 받침으로 쓰세요.
examples.en: Grandmother doesn't throw away a chipped small dish and uses it as a plant saucer.

explain: 간장, 초장, 쌈장 같은 양념을 조금 덜어 담는 작은 그릇이에요. '종지부'의 '종지'와 소리만 같고 서로 다른 말이에요. 보통 '간장 종지'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is a small dish for sauces such as soy sauce, vinegar-chili sauce or ssamjang. It only sounds the same as the '종지' in '종지부' (full stop) and is a different word. People usually say '간장 종지'.

examples.en: This bus's final stop is Seoul Station.
Please wake me when we reach the last stop.

examples.ko: 여행의 종착지가 어디인지 아직 정하지 못했어요.
examples.en: I haven't decided where the trip will end yet.
The train has almost reached its final stop.

examples.ko: 인생의 종착지가 어디일지 가끔 생각해 봐요.
examples.en: Sometimes I wonder where life's final destination will be.

examples.ko: 이 지하철은 종착지까지 한 시간 넘게 걸려요.
examples.en: This subway takes over an hour to reach the last stop.

explain: 버스나 지하철에서는 '종점', '종착역'이라는 말을 더 많이 써요. '종착지'는 긴 여행이나 인생의 마지막 목적지처럼 비유로도 쓰기 좋아요. 반대말은 '출발지'예요.
explain_en: For buses and subways, '종점' and '종착역' are more common. '종착지' also works well as a metaphor for the end of a long journey or of life. Its opposite is '출발지' (starting point).

examples.en: That player ran all over the field without restraint.

examples.ko: 새로 온 기자가 현장을 종횡무진 뛰어다녀요.
examples.en: The new reporter dashes around the scene in every direction.
He performed with tireless energy on stage.
The kids run around the playground in every direction.

examples.ko: 이 배우는 영화와 드라마를 넘나들며 종횡무진 활동해요.
examples.en: This actor works tirelessly, moving between films and dramas.
I'm proud of my junior, who is performing so brilliantly.

explain: 주로 '종횡무진 활약하다', '종횡무진 누비다'처럼 부사처럼 써서 거침없이 움직이는 모습을 칭찬해요. 한 곳에 머물지 않고 여러 분야나 장소를 오가는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is mostly used like an adverb, as in '종횡무진 활약하다' or '종횡무진 누비다', to praise someone moving without restraint. It has the feeling of ranging across many places or fields instead of staying in one.

examples.en: Moonlight pours down in a stream.
The cup tipped over and the water gushed out.
Coins came rolling out of the bag all at once.
Rainwater streams down from the roof.
I poured the marbles into the box with a rattle.
I poured the rice into the jar in a rush.

explain: 물, 구슬, 쌀, 동전처럼 작은 것들이 한꺼번에 쏟아지거나 흘러내릴 때 써요. '쏟아지다', '흘러내리다', '굴러 나오다' 같은 동사와 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is used when small things such as water, marbles, rice or coins pour or flow out all at once. It goes well with verbs like '쏟아지다', '흘러내리다' and '굴러 나오다'.

examples.en: I was on edge while waiting for my interview result.
My child isn't home yet this late and I can't sit still.

examples.ko: 시험 발표 전날 밤에는 좌불안석으로 잠도 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The night before the results, I was so uneasy I couldn't sleep.

examples.ko: 회의 내내 좌불안석이던 신입 사원이 결국 일어났어요.
examples.en: The new employee, who had been fidgeting all through the meeting, finally stood up.
He just stared at his phone with an uneasy face.
When the boss arrived, the staff became uneasy.

explain: 걱정, 긴장, 미안함 때문에 가만히 있지 못할 때 써요. '안절부절못하다'와 가깝지만 한자어라서 글이나 조금 격식 있는 말에 더 어울려요. 보통 '좌불안석이다', '좌불안석으로'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is used when worry, tension or guilt keeps you from sitting still. It is close to '안절부절못하다' but, being Sino-Korean, fits writing or somewhat formal speech better. It is usually used as '좌불안석이다' or '좌불안석으로'.

examples.ko: 정부는 이 문제를 더는 좌시하지 않겠다고 밝혔어요.
examples.en: The government said it will no longer stand idly by on this issue.

examples.ko: 쓰레기 무단 투기를 좌시하면 동네가 지저분해져요.
examples.en: If we let illegal dumping slide, the neighborhood gets dirty.

examples.ko: 주민들은 불법 주차를 좌시할 수 없다고 말했어요.
examples.en: The residents said they can't overlook illegal parking.

examples.ko: 시민들이 이런 일을 좌시하지 않을 거예요.
examples.en: Citizens will not stand by and let this happen.
You are responsible for having looked the other way even though you knew of the wrongdoing.

examples.ko: 회사가 직원의 불만을 좌시해서는 안 돼요.
examples.en: A company must not ignore its employees' complaints.

explain: 거의 '좌시하지 않겠다', '좌시할 수 없다'처럼 부정과 함께 뉴스나 성명서에서 써요. 말할 때는 '그냥 두고 보지 않겠다', '가만있지 않겠다'처럼 풀어서 말해요.
explain_en: It is almost always used with a negative, as in '좌시하지 않겠다' or '좌시할 수 없다', in news and official statements. In speech, people say it more plainly, like '그냥 두고 보지 않겠다' or '가만있지 않겠다'.
